target_customer: Consumers wanting passive lean-back video viewing; no paying customer identified
problem: Finding something worth watching online took effort. Nowmov played an endless stream of popular YouTube clips with no choosing required.
business_model: free consumer video site, no revenue model found (advertising likely but unstated)

founders.name: Thomas Pun
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch May 2010 calls him a longtime Apple engineer.

founders.name: James Felix Black
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch May 2010 names James Black as a longtime Apple engineer.

founders.name: David Kelso
previous_startups: two earlier companies, not named by TechCrunch
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as a former founder.

competitors.name: Magma
competitors.what: Video curation service, described as not really lean-back

competitors.name: YouTube
competitors.what: Platform improving its own recommendation algorithms to keep viewers watching

technical_complexity.rationale: A site that scanned Twitter links to YouTube videos and played them in a stream. Founders were video engineers, but the product itself was light.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on YouTube content and Twitter data, with no lock-in; anyone could copy the idea in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YouTube was already improving recommendations in 2010. No acquirer or later fate for Nowmov was found.

market_need_then: Online video viewing was growing fast in 2010, and TechCrunch described a gap for effortless passive viewing. Demand evidence was mostly the founders' and Kutcher's own premise.

branding.domain_note: nowmov.com no longer resolves in the research environment; the site appears to be gone.

identity.visual_style: Minimal player page with pause, next and share controls per TechCrunch.

branding.community_and_virality: Ashton Kutcher's backing and idea prompt drew launch press. A 2011 iPad app called Nowbox, founded by Thomas Pun, may be related but this is unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: One launch article with celebrity backing, then little trace; the name echoes other 'now' brands.

outcome_analysis: Nowmov launched in May 2010 with Ashton Kutcher and several angels behind it, built by two Apple video engineers and a repeat founder. The YC page lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price was found, and no later coverage exists beyond a possibly related 2011 iPad app called Nowbox. The cause of its end and the exit terms are not public, so no factor is assigned.
notes: Exit status Acquired comes from the YC directory only; two searches found no acquirer, so type is acquisition with null date and acquirer. CB Insights shows about 20K total across rounds and a last round dated Nov 2012; this is a single aggregator figure and unverified, so not recorded. The funding amount in 2010 was not stated by TechCrunch; the round has a null amount. Funding was cross-checked only against the CB Insights listing naming Y Combinator. Nowbox may be a successor but is unconfirmed. nowmov.com did not resolve (site dead).
